paper.core_task: Analyzing gating mechanisms in softmax attention for performance, stability, and attention dynamics

contributions.name: Systematic investigation of gating positions in softmax attention
contributions.author_claim_text: we introduce gating at distinct positions (Fig. 1): after the query (G 4 ), key (G 3 ), and value projections (G 2 ); following the Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) outputs (G 1 ); and after the final dense
contributions.description: A systematic exploration of applying gating at five different positions within the multi-head attention layer to evaluate their effects on model performance.

contributions.name: Analysis of non-linearity and sparsity in gating effectiveness
contributions.author_claim_text: We identify two factors contributing to the efficacy of gating: (i) Non-Linearity... (ii) Sparsity... the pronounced sparsity of the gating scores is another crucial factor, introducing input-dependent sparsity to SDPA outputs
contributions.description: An analysis demonstrating that gating improves performance by introducing non-linearity between linear layers and creating input-dependent sparsity, which mitigates attention sinks.

contributions.name: Dense and MoE model evaluation with gating
contributions.author_claim_text: We conduct experiments on both MoE models (15B total parameters with 2.54B activated, 15A2B) and dense models (1.7B total parameters).
contributions.description: Empirical validation of gating mechanisms across both dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model architectures, demonstrating consistent benefits.
